multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts
subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts

concepts.why: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis) and a high white blood cell count with a predominance of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis are indicative of leukemia, and the specific findings are most consistent with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.

The severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots are suggestive of leptomeningeal involvement, which can be seen in the context of metastatic disease, including Leptomeningeal Metastases.

While less likely given the acute presentation, the presence of leukemia cutis and an elevated white blood cell count could also be seen in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia, although the cell differential would typically show a higher percentage of lymphocytes.

The presence of leukemia cutis and a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid could also suggest Acute Myeloid Leukemia, which can present with neurological symptoms due to leptomeningeal involvement.

The neurological symptoms and signs, including severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening of the lumbosacral nerve roots, could be indicative of lymphoma, particularly if there is central nervous system involvement.

rationales.F01: Subacute progressive weakness is more typical of leukemia or lymphoma than other conditions.
rationales.F04: Severe flaccid quadriparesis is a strong indicator of a severe neurological condition such as leukemia or leptomeningeal metastases.
rationales.F06: Violaceous cutaneous lesions are highly suggestive of leukemia cutis, which is a strong indicator of leukemia.
rationales.F09: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots is more typical of leptomeningeal metastases or leukemia.
rationales.F11: A high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid is highly suggestive of leukemia or lymphoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with violaceous cutaneous lesions, severe flaccid quadriparesis, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing 98% atypical cells/blasts is most consistent with Acute Myeloid Leukemia, which is known to cause leukemia cutis and central nervous system involvement.
